land.text: central Arabia (Najd and the Yamama), the Ma'add confederation's land, over which Himyar installed Hujr

predecessors.note: Kinda page: 'In the mid-5th century, part of the Kinda, with support from Himyar, migrated' and came to dominate the Ma'add; the Himyarite Kingdom page dates Himyarite rule over Ma'add 'around the mid-fifth century'. The land is the Ma'add tribes', not a state's, so the real predecessor is nobody; Himyar is the sponsor.

capitals.name: Qaryat al-Faw (Qaryat Dhat Kahl)
capitals.note: Kingdom of Kindah page: capital at Qaryat al-Faw, on the southern edge of the Tuwayq range, after the Aksumite expansion displaced the Kinda in the late 2nd century AD. The Qaryat al-Faw page says the Kinda 'abandoned it around 300 AD to settle in Hadhramaut', so for the Hujrid kingdom of 450-528 the seat is unsettled (the Kinda page names none; Hujr died at Batn Aqil). Coordinates from the Qaryat al-Faw page.

correction.text: the Kindite realm in central Arabia: 'Najd (Batn Aqil), Yamama (Hajar, al-Mushaqqar)' under the Banu Akil al-Murar (Kingdom of Kindah page); Amr al-Maqsur 'ruled the Najd part' and Mu'awiya al-Jawn 'the Yamama' (Kinda page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The Kinda page puts the kingdom in the Najd and Yamama; the Kingdom of Kindah page adds the 'Tihama/Jabal Shammar regions'. The gazetteer's Nejd (about 551,000 km2, bbox 39-48 E, 19-29 N) is the reading; the real hold was a tribal hegemony over the Ma'add confederation, so the edge is soft and the interior was not uniformly ruled. The original homeland, Ghamr Dhi Kinda about 90 km north-west of Mecca (Kingdom page), is not included.

region.text: the Kindite realm in central Arabia: 'Najd (Batn Aqil), Yamama (Hajar, al-Mushaqqar)' under the Banu Akil al-Murar (Kingdom of Kindah page); Amr al-Maqsur 'ruled the Najd part' and Mu'awiya al-Jawn 'the Yamama' (Kinda page)

ledger.note: c. 450: Hujr, a Kindite prince backed by Himyar, founds the Banu Akil al-Murar kingdom over the Ma'add of central Arabia. Kinda page: 'In the mid-5th century, part of the Kinda, with support from Himyar, migrated' into central and northern Arabia; the Himyarite king gave Ma'add's kingship to Hujr. The year is the first of 'mid-5th century' (and the Kingdom of Kindah infobox says 'c. 3rd CE-c. 528 CE', which counts the earlier Kinda).

region.text: the Kindite realm in central Arabia: 'Najd (Batn Aqil), Yamama (Hajar, al-Mushaqqar)' under the Banu Akil al-Murar (Kingdom of Kindah page); Amr al-Maqsur 'ruled the Najd part' and Mu'awiya al-Jawn 'the Yamama' (Kinda page)

ledger.note: c. 528: al-Harith ibn Amr, the greatest Kindite king, is slain and the kingdom breaks up. Kinda page: 'There, in 528, he was slain by the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III'; the kingdom 'lasted until the mid-6th century', by when its rulers had been killed or had fled to Hadramawt. Kingdom of Kindah infobox ends c. 528. The Kinda lost the Yamama at Shi'b Jabala, dated c. 550, 570 or 580. No page names a successor state.

wars.name: Kindite capture of al-Hira
wars.outcome: Al-Harith captured al-Hira, ruled it briefly, then turned to the Byzantines.
wars.note: Kingdom of Kindah page: al-Harith captured al-Hira 'sometime during the reign' of Kavad I (498-531). The years given here are the start of that reign and al-Harith's death, a window, not dated fighting. Hira is not in the gazetteer and the land is not claimed.

wars.name: Kindite-Lakhmid war (death of al-Harith)
wars.outcome: Al-Harith was slain by the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III (or by the Banu Kalb); the Kindite kingdom fell apart.
wars.note: Kinda page: 'in 528, he was slain by the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III'; the Kingdom of Kindah page says al-Mundhir III 'or the Banu Kalb'.

certainty.note: A tribal hegemony in the desert interior: no frontier is described by any page. Soft throughout.
